body:
There is an invariant in JS that [ArrayBufferByteLength](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/structured-data.html#sec-arraybufferbytelength) can only be called on ArrayBuffers which are not detached. Callers of the "byte length" operation in other specs may not be respecting that invariant. (Is there any way to know what those callers are? I checked a couple likely specs and the only one I found which is passing an ArrayBuffer is [WebNN](https://www.w3.org/TR/webnn/#validate-buffer-with-descriptor), which is indeed not guarding against detached buffers.)

It would be good to either handle that here (by throwing or returning 0) or at the very least to note that invariant for callers.

body:
It's weird for this to treat detached and out of bounds differently - nothing in ecma262 does that. My preference would be to rectify this by replacing this "is detached" check to "is out of bounds", and have "is out of bounds" cover both detached and out of bounds ([like it does in ecma262](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ordinary-and-exotic-objects-behaviours.html#sec-istypedarrayoutofbounds)).

In fact probably the right thing is to replace _every_ detachedness check with an OOB check covering both possibilities.

body:
With tc39/ecma262#3972, "byte length" and "byte offset" now return 0 for out-of-bounds `DataView`s too (3ae5bf0, 4496852), so detached and out-of-bounds views are both reported as having a byte length of 0.

That means this step didn't need an "is out of bounds" check at all: I've removed the "is detached" check, so the existing "If |length| is 0" check now covers both cases uniformly (bfe0173).

As for the other detachedness checks, I went through them, but I don't think any of them should become an out-of-bounds check:
* "Byte length" of a plain `ArrayBuffer` or `SharedArrayBuffer` checks `IsDetachedBuffer`, since buffers themselves can't be out of bounds.
* "Detached", "transferable", "transfer" and "detach" are about detaching and transferring the buffer itself, where being out of bounds doesn't matter. (A view on a shrunk buffer doesn't stop that buffer from being transferred.)
* "Write" into an `ArrayBufferView` already asserts that the view is not out of bounds, which implies it's not detached either.
